mechanism: Stimulant anthraquinone laxatives deplete serum potassium, sensitising cardiac Na+/K+-ATPase binding sites to digoxin.
description: Prolonged or excessive senna laxative use causes potassium loss that markedly increases digoxin toxicity and life-threatening arrhythmias.
evidenceNote: Health Canada NHP monograph requires consulting a practitioner if taking heart medications or products contributing to electrolyte imbalance.

mechanism: Synergistic renal and intestinal potassium excretion.
description: Combining senna anthraquinones with potassium-wasting diuretics (furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide) compounds renal and colonic potassium loss, risking severe hypokalemia and arrhythmia (EMA).

mechanism: Additive gastrointestinal and renal potassium wasting.
description: Taking senna with loop diuretics compounds potassium and fluid depletion, increasing weakness, cramps, and cardiac rhythm risk.
evidenceNote: Health Canada monograph explicitly flags diuretics due to electrolyte imbalance risk.

mechanism: Synergistic colonic and distal-tubular potassium loss.
description: Thiazide diuretics combined with stimulant senna laxatives increase the risk of clinically significant hypokalemia.
evidenceNote: Based on Health Canada NHP electrolyte imbalance warnings.

mechanism: Mineralocorticoid activity of corticosteroids adds to anthraquinone-induced potassium excretion.
description: Systemic corticosteroids paired with regular senna use amplify potassium depletion and electrolyte disturbance.
evidenceNote: Health Canada senna monograph lists corticosteroids as requiring practitioner consultation.

mechanism: Potential additive antiplatelet or anticoagulant activity, or altered anticoagulant metabolism noted in official regulatory safety guidance.
description: Concurrent use may alter platelet aggregation or anticoagulant response and elevate bleeding risk. Clinical monitoring (including INR checks when taking warfarin) and medical supervision are recommended before combining.

mechanism: Fibrinolytic enzyme exposure paired with COX-1 mucosal prostaglandin suppression.
description: Combining serrapeptase with NSAID anti-inflammatories adds to gastrointestinal irritation and mucosal bleeding risk.
evidenceNote: Health Canada explicitly flags anti-inflammatory medications and GI ulcer warnings.

mechanism: Additive proteolytic breakdown of fibrin and clot destabilization.
description: Serrapeptase exhibits fibrinolytic activity that can increase bleeding risk when paired with warfarin or antiplatelets.
evidenceNote: Health Canada serrapeptase monograph requires practitioner consult before use with blood thinners or before surgery.

mechanism: Baicalin and other flavonoids bind GABA-A receptors, potentially creating additive sedation with benzodiazepines.
description: Skullcap may enhance sedative effects of CNS depressant medications.

mechanism: Physical viscous mucilage barrier impairing tablet dissolution and mucosal drug diffusion in the gastrointestinal tract.
description: The thick mucilage in slippery elm coats the digestive tract and can slow or reduce the intestinal absorption of oral medications if taken simultaneously. Separate dosing by 1 to 2 hours.

mechanism: Pharmacodynamic immunostimulation.
description: Spirulina stimulates immune-cell activity in preclinical/clinical immunology studies and MSK advises caution with transplant immunosuppressants or autoimmune flares (distinct from corticosteroids used medically to treat hepatitis).

mechanism: CYP3A4 induction accelerates benzodiazepine metabolism.
description: St. John's Wort may reduce alprazolam efficacy through increased metabolism.
source: PubMed — Planta Med 2005: No relevant interaction with alprazolam, caffeine, tolbutamide, and digoxin by treatment w

mechanism: Potential additive antiplatelet or anticoagulant activity, or altered anticoagulant metabolism noted in official regulatory safety guidance.
description: * Warfarin, an anticoagulant (blood thinner) Consult a healthcare professional and monitor coagulation parameters (such as INR or bleeding signs) when combining with anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy.

mechanism: Both agents raise synaptic serotonin: St. John's Wort inhibits serotonin reuptake while SSRIs block it, and St. John's Wort also induces CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. The additive serotonergic effect can reach toxic levels.
description: St. John's Wort combined with SSRI antidepressants can cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening reaction with agitation, confusion, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, and hyperthermia. The combination should be avoided.

mechanism: Additive serotonergic activity from both compounds increasing synaptic serotonin.
description: Risk of serotonin syndrome when combined with citalopram, an SSRI antidepressant.

mechanism: Strong induction of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein increases cyclosporine metabolism and efflux, reducing plasma levels by up to 50%.
description: St. John's Wort dramatically reduces cyclosporine blood levels, potentially causing organ transplant rejection. This interaction has caused documented transplant failures.
source: PubMed — J Vet Pharmacol Ther 2012: Time-course effects of St John's wort on the pharmacokinetics of cyclosporine in dogs: int

mechanism: Induction of P-glycoprotein in the intestine reduces digoxin absorption and increases renal excretion.
description: St. John's Wort reduces digoxin levels by approximately 25%, potentially reducing its cardiac effects.
source: PubMed — Ther Drug Monit 2008: Herbal supplements and therapeutic drug monitoring: focus on digoxin immunoassays and inte

mechanism: Both St. John's Wort and SSRIs increase serotonin levels. Combined use leads to excessive serotonergic activity in the central nervous system, risking serotonin syndrome.
description: Combining St. John's Wort with SSRIs can cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition characterized by agitation, confusion, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, and hyperthermia.

mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein induction dramatically increases drug metabolism and decreases absorption.
description: St. John's Wort reduces HIV protease inhibitor levels by 57% or more, potentially leading to treatment failure, viral rebound, and drug resistance.

mechanism: Immunostimulant or immunomodulatory botanicals may theoretically oppose the therapeutic action of immunosuppressive medications.
description: Do not use if you are taking antidepressants, anxiolytics, anti-cancer, cardiovascular, contraceptive medications, blood thinners, anti-HIV agents and/or medications to suppress the immune system (Brinker 2010; Barnes et al. 2007; Bradley 2006; Mills and Bone 2005; Murphy et al. 2005; Frye et al. 2004; Hebert et al. 2004; Jiang et al. 2004; Mueller et al. 2004; Smith et al. 2004; Sparreboom et al. 2004; Tannergren et al. 2004; Wichtl 2004; Alscher and Klotz 2003; Bauer et al. 2003; Dresser et al. 2003; ESCOP 2003; Hall et al. 2003; Hoffmann 2003; Pfrunder et al. 2003; Schwarz et al. 2003; Bolley 2002; Gorski et al. 2002; Mathijssen et al. 2002; Ahmed et al. 2001; De Maat et al. 2001; Moschella and Jaber 2001; Roby et al. 2001; Sugimoto et al. 2001; Turton-Weeks 2001; Wang et al. 2001; Barone et al. 2000; Durr et al. 2000; Karliova et al. 2000; Mai et al. 2000; Piscitelli et al. 2000; Ruschitzka et al. 2000; Ernst 1999; Johne et al. 1999; Maurer et al. 1999; Rey and Walter 1998). Consult a specialist before use if taking immunosuppressive therapy.

mechanism: CYP3A4 induction increases conversion of irinotecan to inactive metabolites.
description: St. John's Wort reduces irinotecan levels by approximately 42%, severely compromising chemotherapy effectiveness.
source: PubMed — Curr Drug Metab 2007: A mechanistic study on altered pharmacokinetics of irinotecan by St. John's wort.
evidenceNote: A mechanistic study shows St John's wort altering irinotecan pharmacokinetics.

mechanism: Induction of CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 accelerates omeprazole metabolism.
description: St. John's Wort may reduce the effectiveness of omeprazole by increasing its metabolism.
source: PubMed — Clin Pharmacol Ther 2005: Additional discussions regarding the altered metabolism and transport of omeprazole after

mechanism: Hyperforin in St. John's Wort induces CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, increasing metabolism of ethinyl estradiol and progestins, reducing their plasma levels by up to 50%.
description: St. John's Wort significantly reduces the effectiveness of birth control pills, leading to breakthrough bleeding and unintended pregnancies. Multiple case reports of contraceptive failure exist.
source: PubMed — J Am Pharm Assoc (2003) 2007: Drug interaction between oral contraceptives and St. John's Wort: appropriateness of advic

mechanism: Both compounds increase synaptic serotonin levels through different mechanisms, causing dangerous serotonergic excess.
description: St. John's Wort combined with paroxetine can cause serotonin syndrome. This combination should be strictly avoided.

mechanism: Hyperforin-mediated PXR activation induces hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 and P-gp efflux, accelerating saquinavir clearance.
description: St. John's wort (hyperforin) potently induces CYP3A4 and intestinal P-glycoprotein, markedly reducing plasma concentrations of HIV protease inhibitors including saquinavir (as well as indinavir and ritonavir-boosted regimens), risking loss of HIV viral suppression and antiretroviral drug resistance. Contraindicated.

mechanism: Additive serotonergic effects through inhibition of serotonin reuptake by both agents.
description: Concurrent use with sertraline significantly increases the risk of serotonin syndrome. Multiple case reports document this dangerous interaction.

mechanism: CYP3A4 induction increases simvastatin metabolism.
description: St. John's Wort reduces simvastatin levels by approximately 50%, significantly diminishing its cholesterol-lowering effect.
source: PubMed — Clin Pharmacol Ther 2001: Different effects of St John's wort on the pharmacokinetics of simvastatin and pravastatin

mechanism: CYP3A4 induction increases tacrolimus metabolism, drastically lowering blood concentrations.
description: St. John's Wort significantly reduces tacrolimus levels, risking organ rejection in transplant patients.
source: PubMed — Clin Pharmacol Drug Dev 2024: Effect of Tacrolimus Formulation (Prolonged-Release vs Immediate-Release) on Its Susceptib

mechanism: Induction of CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 enzymes accelerates warfarin metabolism, reducing anticoagulant effect.
description: St. John's Wort decreases warfarin effectiveness by increasing its metabolism, potentially leading to subtherapeutic INR levels and increased risk of blood clots.
source: PubMed — Br J Clin Pharmacol 2004: Effect of St John's wort and ginseng on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of warfa
evidenceNote: St John's wort significantly increased clearance of both warfarin enantiomers and reduced the anticoagulant effect; ginseng did not.

mechanism: Synergistic myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase inhibition.
description: Strophanthus contains ouabain/strophanthin cardiac glycosides that directly compound digoxin toxicity and induce fatal heart block.

mechanism: Hypokalemia-potentiated cardiac glycoside toxicity.
description: Hypokalemia from diuretics severely amplifies strophanthin ventricular arrhythmia risk.

mechanism: Thymol- and carvacrol-mediated inhibition of cyclooxygenase platelet thromboxane synthesis.
description: Concentrated thyme extracts and thymol essential oil show antiplatelet activity in vitro and may theoretically increase bleeding susceptibility with blood thinners at medicinal doses.

mechanism: Suspected additive hepatotoxic risk in vulnerable individuals.
description: Because rare liver injury cases have been linked to tongkat ali products, avoid pairing with potentially hepatotoxic doses of medications.
evidenceNote: Health Canada (NIH 2024) prohibits use in liver disorders and LiverTox rates it Likelihood D.

mechanism: Human pharmacokinetic study demonstrated lower propranolol absorption and Cmax when taken concurrently.
description: Co-administering Tongkat ali (Eurycoma longifolia) reduces oral bioavailability and peak levels of propranolol.
evidenceNote: Health Canada monograph explicitly warns users taking propranolol (Salman et al. 2010).

mechanism: Curcumin inhibits platelet aggregation and thromboxane synthesis, adding to aspirin's irreversible COX-1 inhibition — an additive antiplatelet effect.
description: Combining turmeric (curcumin) with aspirin may increase the risk of bleeding. Both inhibit platelet aggregation through different pathways, and case reports describe prolonged bleeding time with concurrent use.

mechanism: Curcumin inhibits platelet aggregation through COX and thromboxane inhibition, adding to clopidogrel's antiplatelet effect.
description: Turmeric may increase the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel, raising bleeding risk.

mechanism: Curcumin may improve insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism, adding to metformin's hypoglycemic effects.
description: Turmeric may enhance the blood sugar-lowering effect of metformin, with potential benefit but requiring monitoring.

mechanism: Curcumin may inhibit P-glycoprotein and BCRP transporters, reducing sulfasalazine efflux and increasing its absorption.
description: Turmeric may increase sulfasalazine blood levels, potentially increasing its therapeutic effects and side effects.

mechanism: Curcumin inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, potentially reducing tacrolimus metabolism and increasing absorption.
description: Curcumin may increase tacrolimus blood levels, requiring monitoring in transplant patients.
source: PubMed — Eur J Hosp Pharm 2023: Spice-drug interactions: a case report on the use of turmeric, curry and ginger in a renal
evidenceNote: A case report in a renal transplant patient describes turmeric, curry and ginger use alongside tacrolimus and reports concentrations unchanged during the period described. Grade lowered from moderate: the published record does not show harm.

mechanism: Curcumin inhibits platelet aggregation and may inhibit CYP enzymes involved in warfarin metabolism, potentially increasing warfarin levels.
description: Turmeric and curcumin may enhance anticoagulant effects of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk.
source: PubMed — Pharm Biol 2021: The influence of Javanese turmeric (Curcuma xanthorrhiza) on the pharmacokinetics of warfa

mechanism: Altered renal electrolyte and water clearance affects steady-state lithium levels.
description: Uva ursi exhibits mild aquaretic/diuretic action and can impair renal lithium excretion if dehydration occurs.
evidenceNote: Health Canada notes short-term use limitations and organ-function precautions.

mechanism: Both valerian and alcohol enhance GABAergic inhibition in the central nervous system.
description: Valerian combined with alcohol may cause additive CNS depression, increasing drowsiness and impaired coordination.

mechanism: Additive GABA-A receptor modulation causing enhanced CNS depression.
description: Concurrent use of valerian and alprazolam may lead to excessive sedation and respiratory depression.

mechanism: Additive GABAergic effects enhance CNS depression.
description: Combining valerian with lorazepam increases risk of excessive sedation and CNS depression.

mechanism: Both compounds enhance GABA activity, potentially creating excessive sedation.
description: Valerian may enhance sedative effects of zolpidem, increasing drowsiness and next-day impairment.

mechanism: Vitex acts on dopamine D2 receptors, potentially creating additive effects with dopamine agonists.
description: Vitex has dopaminergic activity and may interact with dopamine-related medications.

mechanism: Potential phytoestrogenic, dopaminergic, or endocrine receptor interaction with hormone replacement therapy noted in regulatory monograph warnings.
description: In several short term clinical trials, chaste tree in conventional oral doses was typically described as having no or only mild adverse side effects, with no mention of either hepatotoxicity or ALT elevations. Furthermore, in multiple large series of drug and herbal product induced liver injury no cases of chaste tree associated injury have been reported. Single case reports of liver injury with jaundice attributed to chaste tree have been reported to manufacturers, but other possible diagnoses were not adequately excluded. Thus, there is little evidence that chaste tree in conventional oral doses causes clinically apparent liver injury with jaundice in humans. Because of its possible hormonal effects, use of high doses in persons with preexisting liver disease or cirrhosis is discouraged, and its use is not recommended in pregnant or breastfeeding women, or in women on birth control or hormone replacement. Consult a healthcare professional before combining with hormone replacement therapy.

mechanism: Vitex modulates prolactin and progesterone through dopaminergic action on the pituitary, potentially affecting contraceptive hormonal balance.
description: Vitex's hormonal effects may theoretically interfere with hormonal contraceptive effectiveness.

mechanism: Additive Na+/K+-ATPase inhibition.
description: Euonymus atropurpureus bark contains cardiac glycosides (euonymoside) causing additive cardiac toxicity alongside digoxin.

mechanism: Potential additive antiplatelet or anticoagulant activity, or altered anticoagulant metabolism noted in official regulatory safety guidance.
description: Concurrent use may alter platelet aggregation or anticoagulant response and elevate bleeding risk. Clinical monitoring (including INR checks when taking warfarin) and medical supervision are recommended before combining.

mechanism: Both white willow salicin derivatives and aspirin act through salicylic acid pathways that inhibit cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes and reduce gastric mucosal protection.
description: Concurrent use of willow bark with aspirin may produce additive salicylate effects, increasing the risk of gastrointestinal irritation, ulceration, and bleeding.

mechanism: Additive inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis and platelet function by willow-derived salicylates and NSAIDs compounds gastrointestinal and hemorrhagic risk.
description: Combining willow bark with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) may increase the risk of gastrointestinal upset, mucosal ulceration, and bleeding.

mechanism: Salicylates inhibit platelet aggregation via cyclooxygenase blockade and can displace warfarin from plasma protein binding sites.
description: Willow bark contains salicin, which is metabolized to salicylic acid and may increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, raising the risk of bleeding and elevated INR.

mechanism: Inhibition of CYP2C9-mediated S-warfarin metabolism.
description: Multiple documented clinical case reports show goji berry / wolfberry (Lycium barbarum) tea, juice, and concentrates sharply elevated INR and caused serious bleeding in stable warfarin patients (MSK/PubMed). Avoid.

mechanism: Thujone is a GABA-A receptor antagonist that may reduce seizure threshold and oppose anticonvulsant drug effects.
description: Wormwood contains thujone which may lower the seizure threshold and counteract anticonvulsant medications.
